name: Willis Johnson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025)
forbes_bio: Willis Johnson is the founder of Dallas-based Copart, a leader in online auctions for used and totaled cars; he owns about 6% of the stock.
Johnson founded the company out of a single lot in Vallejo, California in 1982 after several years operating a dismantling yard near Sacramento.
He took the company public in 1994 and expanded across the country; Copart now has more than 200 locations in 11 countries.

Johnson stepped down as CEO in 2010 and handed over the reins to his son-in-law, Jay Adair, who first joined Copart in 1989 at age 19. (Adair stepped down as CEO in 2024 and is now executive chairman.)
Before starting Copart, Johnson worked at a Safeway grocery store and at his father's scrapyard in California.
forbes_facts: Johnson was drafted into the Vietnam War and was awarded a Purple Heart for his service.
Johnson owns a large collection of classic cars at his home outside Nashville, Tennessee; his prized possession is a black 1955 Chevrolet.

forbes_bio: William Teh Lee Pang is the son of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who founded Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank and chaired it for several decades.
Teh Hong Piow founded the bank in 1966. He died in December 2022 at age 92.
n addition to Malaysia, the bank serves millions of customers across Cambodia, China, Hong Kong, Sri Lanka and Vietnam.
The late Teh owned a substantial minority stake in the bank as well as in the listed insurance business, LPI Capital.

name: Jian Jun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2021-2025)
forbes_bio: Jian Jun is the chairwoman of biomedical supplier Imeik Technology Development, which makes products like skin fillers and facial implant threads.
Imeik listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020, in an IPO that raised more than $530 million.
Best known for its Hearty filler that treats neck wrinkles, the company has also branched into segments such as skincare products amid heightened competition.
Jian worked for the state-owned China National Cereals Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export early in her career.

name: Zheng Jianjiang

forbes_bio: Zheng Jianjiang is founder and chairman of Aux Group, a conglomerate and controlling shareholder of Ningbo Sanxing Medical Electric.
Zheng cofounded Ninbo Sanxing Medical Electric in 2007 and took it public in Shanghai in 2011.
Ninbo Sanxing supplies power distribution equipment such as smart meters and transformers.
Prior to Aux, Zheng worked at a bankrupt watch parts factory in 1986 with seven other people.

name: Shalom Meckenzie
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Shalom Meckenzie is an Israeli entrepreneur who became the largest shareholder in daily fantasy and sports-betting firm Draft Kings in early 2020.
He secured an 11% stake in Draft Kings when it merged with his company, SBTech.
Meckenzie founded gambling-technology provider SBTech in 2007 and served as a director until May 2014.
DraftKings is an official daily fantasy and sports betting partner of the NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, PGA TOUR and UFC.
Meckenzie spent $11.8 million to acquire a rare CryptoPunk NFT in a June 2021 auction run by Sotheby's.

name: Sundar Pichai
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2018-2019); Wikidata (2021); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Sundar Pichai is CEO of Google parent Alphabet, a position he has held since 2019, when he was tapped to replace Google cofounder Larry Page.
Pichai has worked at Google since 2004, reportedly interviewing for the job the same day Google launched Gmail. He became Google's CEO in 2015.
He holds around 0.02% of Alphabet and has sold more than $500 million worth of shares, before taxes.
Born in Chennai, India, Pichai grew up with limited access to technology but was always interested in how it can create community.
He said that in 1993, his father spent a year's salary on a plane ticket to California so Sundar could attend Stanford.

forbes_bio: Alexander Klyachin owns one of the biggest Russian hotel chains, Azimut, which operates more than 11,000 rooms.

forbes_facts: Klyachin owns the Metropol hotel, which served as the headquarters of the opposition to the Bolsheviks in 1917.
